[quote=dhornaper;59981874][B]That Same Night[/b]

President Fereydun Khan sits at the head of the table in the presidential palace's conference room as he hears from Minister Jalayer Khan about Hydronia's offer to resume the trade agreement.

"The Hydronians confuse me. I don't understand why they're so worried about the EDU. It hardly has any global aspirations unlike THEP. And the offer to resume trade by changing the terms to be unequal is a non-starter. Elesyr is a wealthy continent. I can't just cut them out." President Khan says.

"If I may add," begins Minister Khalil Rahman, "since we struck a trade agreement with Orphogron for uranium, the bulk of the trade agreement, uranium for our future nuclear reactors, has become rather pointless to us."

The President thinks for a moment. "I agree but the price for food has gone up rather uncomfortably ever since the agreement was suspended. Food for the set amount of aluminum we offered is a bad deal for us though. I would rather renegotiate the trade agreement from scratch since they've flouted the old agreement but I'd rather not antagonise them."

After a short pause, he continues. "Minister Jalayer, send a message to Hydronia that although they have flouted the terms of the treaty and attempted to modify the terms, we are willing to renegotiate the treaty from scratch. And send a message to Jomsland discretely. I want to hear from them about the conflict and see if we can negotiate a trade agreement for coal."

"Yes sir," Minister Jalayer responds.

With that, the President dismisses his Ministers and retires for the night.

[quote=bantarus;59982378]Classified Diplomatic Response from the Second Commonwealth of Jomsland 
Sender: Jarl Holmgeir IV. of Reikyawik, Minister of Industry and Chief Economic Advisor
Recipient: The Office of President Fereydun Khan, Dhornaper
Security Clearance: Confidential

To His Excellency President Fereydun Khan,
May the strength of your people and the endurance of your land remain unshaken.
I write to you on behalf of the Althing of the Second Commonwealth of Jomsland and his majesty High King Jorik III., in recognition of your discreet outreach concerning the conflict in Nestorstaat and your interest in initiating trade.
Let me speak plainly.
The recent events concerning the Technocratic Kaiserreich and the situation in Nestorstaat have been widely mischaracterized by foreign observers. The Second Commonwealth of Jomsland viewed the Kaiserreichs war to take Nestor from Sikirsk not as an act of aggression, but as a just and necessary effort to rid native Elseyran soil of foreign subversion and creeping control. We believe in a continental order free from external domination, governed by native powers who understand the regions complex balance and share in its future.
Regarding your interest in coal, Jomsland is well-positioned to supply your industry.Our mines in Marskborg and the Bay of Sverker produce clean-burning coal in volumes sufficient for international trade. We would be open to negotiating a bilateral agreement focused on coal exports in exchange for selected Dhornaperan goods, under fair and predictable terms.
We await your terms.[/quote]

[b][u]Confidential Diplomatic Message to Jomsland[/u][/b]
Sender: [i]President Fereydun Khan of Dhornaper[/i]
To: [i]Minister of Industry Jarl Holmgeir IV. of Reikyawik[/i]

Thank you Minister for your kind words and speedy response.

I am thankful for your explanation of the conflict. I find the situation worrisome and remain rather confused how events between two nations, which could have been settled diplomatically, have escalated to such an extraordinary scale. Dhornaper is, of course, neutral and will not be involved in the conflict. Our current understanding of the situation is very poor.

Regarding trade, Dhornaper has ample natural resources in aluminum, oil, and iron which we are willing to exchange for coal required for our manufacturing industries. We are willing to exchange these or pay money in fair amounts for 20 million tons of coal per year.

I hope this message reaches you well so we can agree a fair and mutually beneficial agreement.
